- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots downward; reduce forecast dip by 10-20% of the spike magnitude.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underpredicts true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% upward bias to first 5 days of forecast.  
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.4 to +0.3 within 3 days), model lags in adjusting; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to underestimate true price; apply 1–3% upward bias to forecast for next 7–10 days.  
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion after 10+ days of trend; if sentiment is flat or mildly negative, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast for days 8–15.
